extracted.intended_audience: applicants, proprietors, professional representatives, EPO examiners/boards, national patent offices and courts
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements under the European Patent Convention governing examination, opposition, appeals, representation, conversion to national procedures, evidence, time limits, amendments and other matters in European patent prosecution and post-grant proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to the Enlarged Board of Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Board of Appeal shall refer any question to the Enlarged Board of Appeal during proceedings if it considers a decision is required to ensure uniform application of the law or because an important point of law arises; the President of the EPO may refer a point of law where two Boards have given different decisions on that question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board rejects a party's request to refer, it must give reasons in its final decision. Decisions of the Enlarged Board referred to in the referral are binding on the Board of Appeal in respect of the appeal in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions based on evidence on which parties had opportunity to comment
rubrics_metrics.description: The decisions of the European Patent Office may only be based on grounds or evidence on which the parties concerned have had an opportunity to present their comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures parties' right to be heard; grounds/evidence introduced without opportunity to comment should not form the basis of decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision limited to text submitted or agreed by applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: The European Patent Office shall consider and decide upon the European patent application or the European patent only in the text submitted to it, or agreed, by the applicant for or proprietor of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPO may not base decisions on text other than that submitted/approved by applicant/proprietor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of facts of the EPO's own motion
rubrics_metrics.description: In proceedings before it, the European Patent Office shall examine the facts of its own motion; it shall not be restricted in this examination to the facts, evidence and arguments provided by the parties and the relief sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPO may raise and investigate issues ex officio but remains subject to parties' rights under Article 113 (opportunity to comment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disregard of late-submitted facts or evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The European Patent Office may disregard facts or evidence which are not submitted in due time by the parties concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely submission is required; late material can be excluded at EPO's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party observations after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Following publication of the European patent application, any person may present observations concerning the patentability of the invention; such observations must be filed in writing and must include a statement of the grounds on which they are based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third parties making observations are not parties to proceedings; observations must be communicated to the applicant/proprietor, who may comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to oral proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral proceedings shall take place either at the instance of the European Patent Office if it considers this to be expedient or at the request of any party to the proceedings, subject to certain limits (e.g., EPO may reject a request for further oral proceedings before the same department where parties and subject are the same).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Section will hold oral proceedings at applicant's request only where it considers this expedient or where it envisages refusing the application. Departments may refuse repeated oral proceedings in identical situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity of oral proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral proceedings (including delivery of the decision) shall be public for Boards of Appeal, Enlarged Board of Appeal, and (after publication of the application) Opposition Divisions, unless the department decides otherwise where public admission could cause serious and unjustified disadvantages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral proceedings before Receiving Section, Examining Divisions and Legal Division are not public; departments may exclude public if justified, particularly to protect a party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Means of taking and obtaining evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: In any proceedings before an Examining Division, an Opposition Division, the Legal Division or a Board of Appeal the means of giving or obtaining evidence shall include hearing the parties; requests for information; production of documents; hearing witnesses; opinions by experts; inspection; sworn statements in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are non-exhaustive means; the department may commission a member to examine the evidence adduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for requiring oral evidence or court assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the EPO considers it necessary for a party, witness or expert to give evidence orally, it shall either issue a summons to appear before it, or request the competent court in the person's country of residence to take such evidence (pursuant to Article 131).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summoned persons may request that evidence be heard by a competent court; EPO may request re-examination under oath by that court and may request presence of a departmental member to question the witness (directly or via the court).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity and uniformity of application/patent text
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicants or proprietors are not the same for different designated Contracting States, they shall be regarded as joint applicants/proprietors for purposes of proceedings; the unity of the application/patent shall not be affected and, in particular, the text shall be uniform for all designated States unless otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains single, uniform text across designated states in EPO proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of decisions and time‑limit communications
rubrics_metrics.description: The European Patent Office shall notify those concerned of decisions and summonses, and of any notice or other communication from which a time limit is reckoned, or of which those concerned must be notified under other provisions; notifications may, where exceptional circumstances require, be given through central industrial property offices of the Contracting States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPO must as a matter of course notify relevant communications; implementing regulations to specify further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation and extension of time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementing Regulations shall specify the manner of computation of time limits and the conditions under which such time limits may be extended, e.g., because the EPO or national authorities are not open to receive documents, or postal services are interrupted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing Regulations also set minima and maxima for time limits to be determined by the EPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further processing after failure to meet a time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is refused or deemed withdrawn following failure to reply within a time limit, the legal consequence shall not ensue or shall be retracted if the applicant requests further processing of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be filed in writing within two months of notification of refusal/deeming; omitted act must be completed within this time; request not deemed filed until fee for further processing is paid; the competent department decides on the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-establishment of rights (restitutio in integrum)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant/proprietor who despite all due care required by the circumstances was unable to observe a time limit shall, upon application, have rights re-established if the non-observance caused refusal, deeming to be withdrawn, revocation, or loss of any other right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must be filed within two months from removal of the cause; omitted act completed within that period; admissible only within one year after expiry of unobserved time limit (with certain deductions/exceptions); must state grounds and facts; fee for re-establishment must be paid; certain time limits are excluded from this Article; third parties who in good faith used the invention during loss of rights may continue such use without payment until publication of re-establishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to amend application/patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions under which a European patent application or patent may be amended in proceedings are laid down in the Implementing Regulations; an applicant shall be allowed at least one opportunity of amending the description, claims and drawings of his own volition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments may not introduce subject-matter extending beyond the content of the application as filed; during opposition proceedings claims may not be amended so as to extend the protection conferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose national filings upon invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Examining Division or Board of Appeal may invite the applicant to indicate, within a period, the States in which he has made national patent applications for the same invention and to give reference numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to reply in due time to such invitation shall lead to the European patent application being deemed withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to general principles of procedural law
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of procedural provisions in the Convention, the European Patent Office shall take into account the principles of procedural law generally recognised in the Contracting States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides gap-filling principle to ensure fair procedure where the Convention is silent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation periods for financial claims against the Organisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights of the Organisation to payment of a fee to the EPO are extinguished after four years from the end of the calendar year in which the fee fell due; rights to refund excess fees are extinguished after four years from the end of the calendar year in which the right arose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interruption rules apply (e.g., by request for payment or reasoned claim); periods may be extended in case judicial proceedings are begun.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of European Patents and public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO shall keep a Register of European Patents containing particulars whose registration is provided for; no entry shall be made prior to publication of the European patent application; the Register shall be open to public inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register entries are tied to publication; provides public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection of files (pre- and post-publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Files relating to unpublished European patent applications shall not be made available without the applicant's consent, except that a person who can prove that the applicant invoked rights under the application against him may obtain inspection prior to publication; following publication files may be inspected on request subject to Implementing Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a divisional or new EP application is published, files of the earlier application may be inspected prior to publication of that application; EPO may communicate certain bibliographic data prior to publication (application number, filing date and priority details, applicant name, title, designated states).

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic publications by the EPO
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO shall periodically publish a European Patent Bulletin (entries from the Register and other prescribed particulars) and an Official Journal containing notices and general information by the President and other information relevant to the Convention or its implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures official dissemination of register entries and administrative information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange of information between EPO and national offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO and central industrial property offices of Contracting States shall, on request, communicate to each other useful information regarding the filing of European or national patent applications and proceedings concerning such applications and patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies also to non-Contracting States and inter-governmental organisations under working agreements; confidentiality rules apply until publication; Administrative Council may permit wider communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and legal cooperation with courts and authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided, the EPO and the courts or authorities of Contracting States shall on request give assistance to each other by communicating information or opening files for inspection; upon receipt of letters rogatory the courts shall undertake necessary enquiries or measures on behalf of the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where EPO lays files open to inspection by courts or prosecutors, Article 128 restrictions do not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange of publications with national offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPO and central industrial property offices shall despatch copies of their respective publications to each other on request and for their own use free of charge; EPO may conclude agreements relating to exchange or supply of publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates mutual access to official publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: General principles of representation (who must/need not be represented)
rubrics_metrics.description: No person shall be compelled to be represented by a professional representative in proceedings established by the Convention, except that natural or legal persons not having residence or principal place of business in a Contracting State must be represented by a professional representative and act through him in all proceedings other than filing the application (subject to Implementing Regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees may represent legal persons resident in a Contracting State if authorised; Implementing Regulations may permit exceptions and set conditions for common representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission to list of professional representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional representation may only be undertaken by representatives whose names appear on a list maintained by the EPO; entry requires that the person be a national of a Contracting State, have place of business or employment in a Contracting State, and have passed the European qualifying examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry effected upon request with certificates; those on the list are entitled to act in all proceedings; President may grant nationality exemption in special circumstances; legal practitioners qualified in a Contracting State and entitled to act in patent matters in that State may also act similarly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Council powers on representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Council may adopt provisions governing qualifications and training for admission to the European qualifying examination, establishment/recognition of an institute for representatives, and disciplinary powers to be exercised by that institute or the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows secondary rules on training, examination conduct, institutes and discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion to national patent procedure (when and how requested)
rubrics_metrics.description: A central industrial property office shall apply the national patent procedure only at the request of the applicant/proprietor and in circumstances such as when the European patent application is deemed withdrawn pursuant to specified Articles, or in other cases provided by national law; the request must be filed within three months after withdrawal/notification and effect under Article 66 lapses if not filed in time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request formalities and time limits are strict; conversion fee/payment rules apply per subsequent Article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and transmittal requirements for conversion requests
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for conversion shall be filed with the EPO specifying the Contracting States desired; not deemed filed until conversion fee paid; EPO shall transmit the request and copy of the files to specified national offices. If the application is deemed withdrawn under certain Articles, request is filed with the national office which shall transmit to other national offices subject to national security; transmittal deadlines (e.g., 20 months) apply or effect under Article 66 lapses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmission delays can cause loss of effect; national security may limit direct transmittal in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements for conversion (national formalities)
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent application transmitted for national procedure shall not be subjected to formal requirements of national law which are different from or additional to those in the Convention. However, a national office may require within not less than two months payment of national application fee and filing of a translation in an official language (and of amended text if appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects applicants from extra national formal demands but allows national offices to require fee payment and translations within a minimum period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for revocation of a European patent
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent may only be revoked under the law of a Contracting State with effect for its territory on grounds including: (a) subject-matter not patentable under Articles 52–57; (b) patent does not disclose the invention sufficiently clearly and completely for it to be carried out by a person skilled in the art; (c) subject-matter extends beyond the content of the application as filed (or earlier application); (d) protection conferred has been extended; (e) proprietor is not entitled under Article 60(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If revocation grounds affect only part of the patent, revocation is pronounced as corresponding limitation; national law may permit limitation by amendment of claims/description/drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-right effect of European and national applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In any designated Contracting State, a European patent application and a European patent shall have the same prior right effect as a national patent application and a national patent; conversely, a national application/patent has the same prior right effect with regard to a European patent in which that State is designated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting States may prescribe whether and on what terms an invention disclosed in both can be protected simultaneously by both national and European applications/patents with same filing/priority date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of provisions to utility models and certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain Articles (e.g., Article 66, 124, 135–137, 139) shall apply to utility models and utility certificates and to applications for them registered or deposited in Contracting States whose laws provide for such models/certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends specified EPC effects to national utility model systems where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal fee years and payment after grant publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal fees for a European patent may only be imposed for the years which follow that referred to in Article 86(4). Any renewal fees falling due within two months after publication of the mention of grant shall be deemed to have been validly paid if paid within that period; additional national fees shall not be charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides transitional rule to avoid double charging immediately after grant publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unitary patent and special agreements between groups of Contracting States
rubrics_metrics.description: Any group of Contracting States that has provided by special agreement that a European patent granted for those States has a unitary character may provide that a European patent may only be granted jointly in respect of all those States; special departments and rules may be set up to carry out additional tasks as agreed by the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group may set up special departments, select committee, lay down representation rules, bear expenses for tasks, and fix common scale of renewal fees with appropriate calculation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: European patent application as object of property and joint designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups of Contracting States may provide that a European patent application for those States may only be transferred/mortgaged/subjected to execution in respect of all States of the group and that these States may be designated jointly (designation of one may constitute designation of all).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affords groups of States ability to harmonize property/transfer/designation rules for unitary or joint designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PCT shall be applied in accordance with this Part: international applications filed under the PCT may be subject to EPO proceedings; provisions of the PCT are applied supplemented by the Convention and, in case of conflict, the PCT prevails. For international applications, the time limit for requesting examination under Article 94(2) of the Convention shall not expire before the time prescribed by PCT Articles 22 or 39 as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An international application for which the EPO acts as designated or elected Office shall be deemed to be a European patent application; references to the PCT include its Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO acting as a receiving Office under the PCT
rubrics_metrics.description: EPO may act as a receiving Office for an international application if the applicant is resident or national of a Contracting State to the Convention in respect of which the PCT has entered into force, or under agreement where applicant is resident/national of a State party to the PCT but not to the Convention, or subject to Administrative Council approval may act for other applicants per agreement with WIPO IB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows EPO to receive international applications in various circumstances subject to treaty and agreement conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and transmittal of international (PCT) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant chooses the EPO as receiving Office, he shall file the international application directly with the EPO; if filed through the national office, that State must ensure timely transmittal to the EPO. Each international application is subject to payment of the transmittal fee payable on filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures correct routing and fee payment for PCT filings when EPO is serving as receiving Office.
